title: Choose the Fireground command composition
question: All three use the approved Fireground Command Board world. Choose the operational arrangement the coded interface should reproduce.

options.label: Evidence Board
options.lineage: tactical worksheet with central evidence chain
options.thesis: A live incident timeline feeds observations and inferences into one guarded action lane.
options.viewport: Snapshot and objectives at left, timeline and evidence graph in the center, approval and rollback controls at right, audit and unit accountability below.
options.risk: It carries the richest evidence story but requires careful responsive collapse.

options.label: Objective Spine
options.lineage: incident objectives as the primary accountability structure
options.thesis: Every service, evidence record, countermeasure, and approval attaches to a named incident objective.
options.viewport: A compact timeline feeds a dominant objective spine whose selected row expands across service, evidence, action, and approval columns.
options.risk: Its clean accountability model shows less causal graph structure at once.

options.label: Command Sectors
options.lineage: signals, impact, and recovery sectors under one command clock
options.thesis: Evidence advances through three operational sectors and converges on one protected action gate.
options.viewport: A left command tower anchors three horizontal evidence sectors, with the approval gate dominating the far edge.
options.risk: The strong sequence can imply more certainty than a branching investigation actually has.
